blocks.text: Blood reaches the kidney through the renal artery, which enters at the hilum and divides into branches that give rise to afferent arterioles. Each afferent arteriole leads into a capillary bed, the glomerulus. Unlike most capillary beds, which drain into venules, the glomerular capillaries drain into an efferent arteriole.

items: The efferent arteriole branches into peritubular capillaries, a dense network round the proximal and distal convoluted tubules in the renal cortex.
In juxtamedullary nephrons the efferent arterioles also give rise to the vasa recta, long straight capillaries in the medulla running parallel to the loops of Henle.

After exchanging materials the capillaries join into venules, the venules into larger veins and finally the renal vein, which leaves at the hilum and drains into the inferior vena cava, returning the filtered blood to the heart.

blocks.title: Did you know?
blocks.text: The kidneys are richly supplied with blood: they receive about 20 to 25% of the total cardiac output.

blocks.alt: Left: one nephron across the cortex and medulla: a wide afferent arteriole enters the glomerulus inside Bowman's capsule and a narrower efferent arteriole leaves; the proximal convoluted tubule leads to the loop of Henle dipping into the medulla, the distal convoluted tubule returns beside the capsule and drains into a collecting duct; peritubular capillaries wrap the tubules and the vasa recta run beside the loop. Right: a flow chart of the blood route from renal artery to inferior vena cava.
blocks.caption: A nephron and the blood supply of the kidney (original diagram after topic 14.1.2).
blocks.long_description: A nephron has a renal corpuscle, the glomerulus (a capillary knot fed by an afferent arteriole) inside the double-walled Bowman's capsule, and a renal tubule: the coiled proximal convoluted tubule, the U-shaped loop of Henle with a descending and an ascending limb, and the coiled distal convoluted tubule, which drains with others into a collecting duct. Blood enters by the renal artery, passes into afferent arterioles, the glomerulus and the efferent arteriole, then the peritubular capillaries round the convoluted tubules and, in juxtamedullary nephrons, the vasa recta beside the loop, before venules and veins return it through the renal vein to the inferior vena cava. About 85% of nephrons are cortical with short loops; juxtamedullary nephrons have long loops deep in the medulla.

blocks.prompt: What is unusual about the vessel that drains the glomerulus, and why does it matter?
blocks.explanation: The glomerulus drains into an arteriole (the efferent arteriole), not a venule. Because the efferent arteriole is narrower than the afferent one, pressure in the glomerulus stays high, which drives filtration (topic 14.1.3).

items: Renal artery, afferent arteriole, glomerulus, efferent arteriole, peritubular capillaries (and vasa recta), venules, renal vein, inferior vena cava.
Kidneys take 20 to 25% of cardiac output.
